comparisons.peer_summary: Citi provides guarantees to credit card partners regarding customer origination volume and minimum revenue targets during the agreement term. If these targets are not met, Citi compensates the partner for the resulting shortfall in payments and revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Both Morgan Stanley and Citigroup disclose specific guarantee obligations that involve potential financial outflows or reversals if certain performance or volume targets are not met. Morgan Stanley notes general partner guarantees including obligations to return previously received performance fee distributions, while Citigroup describes guarantees to credit card partners to compensate for shortfalls in revenue or origination volumes if targets are missed.

sentences.text: See Note 14 for information regarding general partner guarantees, which include potential obligations to return performance fee distributions previously received.

To the extent that such origination and revenue targets are not met, the guarantees serve to compensate the partner for certain payments that otherwise would have been generated in connection with such originations and revenues generated by the program.

comparisons.peer_topic: Investment management fee structure and recognition
comparisons.peer_summary: Investment management fees are based on assets under management and recognized over the service period, while performance-based fees are accrued when reversal probability is remote, typically at the end of the billing period.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley disclose the risk of reversing performance-based fees tied to fund returns. JPM states that performance-based fees are accrued only when the probability of reversal is remote, typically at the end of the billing period, whereas Morgan Stanley explicitly states its unrealized carried interest is at risk of reversing when fund returns fall below specified targets.

sentences.text: The Firm's portion of net cumulative performance-based fees in the form of unrealized carried interest, for which the Firm is not obligated to pay compensation, is at risk of reversing when the returns in certain funds fall below specified performance targets.

The Firm also receives performance-based management fees, which are earned based on exceeding certain benchmarks or other performance targets and are accrued and recognized when the probability of reversal is remote, typically at the end of the related billing period.
